cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Retroactive Permission
cards.instruction: Get approval for something you have already done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like your agreement to dinner for six. We can serve it as a buffet; seated service needs more than two chairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine, people can stand with the soup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not with bowls and nowhere to put them. I've invited them for seven o'clock, so I'll change the soup to something they can eat with one hand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. The invitations are settled; the menu is correctable. Can I have your yes while there is still time to cook?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 corrects seating capacity, A3 corrects standing soup and A5 impatiently distinguishes fixed invitations from fixable menu to seek retrospective agreement.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 soup proposal causes A3 finger-food change; B4 completed-invitation question causes A5 yes and renewed informed approval request.

relationship.evidence: B2 tries to solve seating while B4 legitimately questions being asked after the fact.

heightening.evidence: A5 increases urgency by locating approval before cooking but after invitation, using the consequence exposed by B4.

specificity.evidence: A1 six people and A3 seven oclock now unambiguously distinguish headcount and time.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 terse settled/correctable distinction conveys controlled professional strain while requesting a real answer.
